title: Physics simulation engine (weight, placement, wheels, aero, friction, alignment)
description: Pure, deterministic, dependency-free physics engine: given a full car design (weight, center-of-mass, wheels/rotational inertia, body drag, axle friction, alignment) and a validated track, time-step integrate the run and return a RaceResult (time, outcome, speeds, normal forces, and a closing energy ledger). Grounded in docs/physics-spec.md. No UI. First end-to-end exercise of the TDD build loop. (Scope broadened from weight+placement to full physics per PO decisions 2026-06-02; id renamed weight-placement-engine -> physics-engine 2026-06-02 to match scope.)

open_questions.question: Confirm/replace the geometry constants (A4) and frontal-area defaults (A5).
open_questions.resolution: User accepted the Planner's BSA-typical documented defaults (R_outer 0.595 in, bore-based R_inner placeholder, r_axle 0.045 in nail shank, wheelbase 4.375 in, frontal area approx 1.75 in x 2.5 in). Each lands in constants.py with a sourced comment; R_inner stays a flagged placeholder, tunable if a magnitude looks off. Behavioral ACs remain direction-based so they hold under any reasonable values.

open_questions.question: Confirm the DNF-vs-penalty choice (A2).
open_questions.resolution: User confirmed: an unstable car (d_COM < 0.625 in, front normal force collapses) is a DNF with race_time_s = None (hard crash), returning the partial trajectory and the energy ledger up to the failure. Models the rear-bias tradeoff as a legible cliff rather than a finite penalty.

open_questions.question: Rename the feature id to reflect broadened scope, or keep 0001-weight-placement-engine?
open_questions.resolution: User chose to rename: directory/id is now 0001-physics-engine to match the broadened full-physics scope. All internal references (feature.json, PRD/TRD, physics-spec appendix) updated; planning session_id unchanged.
